title: The Bright Horizon
premise: Petra Whitlock navigates the colony ship Bright Horizon through deep space, secretly maintaining a beacon that broadcasts the location of the four thousand colonists still sleeping in cryo—backups of people already living and loving aboard. When the ship's children begin sharing an identical dream of a drowned Earth calling them home, Petra discovers the beacon was never hers to control: it's a summons from whatever survived below, demanding half the sleepers be woken as repopulation stock for a dying planet. Torn between her loyalty to Captain Ilsa Reyes—the woman she loves—and the truth that their own memories may be fabricated copies, Petra must choose which manifest to transmit before the beacon locks permanently. In the end she sends neither list: she wakes everyone, dooming the mission but freeing humanity to choose its own horizon.
about_author: Odile Nystrom is a former maritime cartographer who traded sea charts for star charts after a decade mapping coastlines that no longer exist. She writes science fiction about people who keep instruments running long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. During a routine maintenance shift, Petra repairs the hold's ancient beacon and discovers its transmission log predates the voyage itself—someone encoded a destination before launch. She hides the finding from Captain Reyes, with whom she's falling in love, and begins quietly investigating the sleeping backups in cryo. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath domestic warmth; the first crack in Petra's trust of her own history.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Children
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Petra and ten-year-old Sefu Okonkwo, who leads the children sharing the same dream of a flooded city singing their names. Sefu's drawings match imagery from the beacon's encrypted files exactly. The colony council dismisses it as mass hysteria, but Reyes privately asks Petra to investigate—forcing Petra to lie to the woman she loves. Emotional beat: innocence colliding with conspiracy; loyalty beginning to strain against truth.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Decoding the beacon fully, Petra learns the truth: the waking crew are copies, and the beacon is a summons from Earth's survivors demanding fifty percent of the sleepers as breeding stock—or the signal will draw scavenger ships instead. Confronted by Reyes, Petra confesses everything; their love fractures under the weight of duty versus honesty. Emotional beat: betrayal, grief, and the terrible clarity that any choice sacrifices someone.

chapters.title: Wake Them All
chapters.summary: Split POV, climax and resolution. With the beacon locking in hours, Petra and a reconciled Reyes race scavengers already inbound. Petra transmits no selection at all—she triggers full revival of all four thousand sleepers, overwhelming the scavengers' capacity and erasing the very category of 'backup.' The novel closes with the whole ship awake, crowded, uncertain, and free, steering toward no one's orders but their own. Emotional beat: costly hope; survival redefined as shared risk rather than sacrifice.
